newsitem.title: GREECE: Divers pull 12 dead from Greek ship, eight missing.
newsitem.headline: Divers pull 12 dead from Greek ship, eight missing.

text.p: Divers have recovered 12 corpses from a Greek cargo ship that capsized last week in bad weather, the merchant marine ministry said on Tuesday.
Eight more people are still missing.
"So far 12 bodies have been found and identified," a ministry spokesman said.
Only one person was rescued and hopes are very slim that any of the missing could still be alive.
The Distos, carrying cement, capsized on Saturday off the port of Kimi on the island of Evia.
The vessel had a crew of 18. The wife and 10-year-old daughter of one crew member and the wife of another were also on board.
The only survivor, 18-year-old nautical college student Christos Anagnostou, told the coastguard two big waves engulfed the ship, which listed and then capsized.
He jumped into the sea and shot flares into the air, helping the coastguard to spot the capsized vessel.
Allegations of delays in the rescue operation prompted a court investigation and the suspension of five coastguard officers on Monday.
Court officials said there was a 10-hour delay in sending help to the vessel and the coastguard officers are accused of delaying telling senior merchant marine ministry officials of the accident.
The ship, owned by the Heracles cement company, was carrying 5,300 tonnes of cement from the central port town of Volos to Piraeus, near Athens.
